title: Modi to Deliver Plenary Address at Kisan Tak Agriculture Conference in Delhi
excerpt: Around 2,000 farmers are expected at the two-day Bharat Mandapam conference on smart farming, AI and climate-resilient crops, held under the theme 'Smart Kisan, Viksit Bharat.'
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi will deliver the plenary address at the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, a two-day event held on November 11-12, IANS reported.
  • Around 2,000 farmers from across India are expected to attend, alongside policymakers, diplomats, industry leaders and agricultural scientists, under the theme "Smart Kisan, Viksit Bharat."
  • Discussions centre on artificial intelligence in farming, precision agriculture, climate-resilient crops and ways to raise farmer incomes.
  • Attendance is by invitation only, according to the India Today Group, which organises the conference.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will deliver the plenary address at the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, according to IANS. The two-day conference, held on November 11 and 12, is organised by the India Today Group and presented by Mahindra Tractors.

The event is expected to bring together around 2,000 farmers from different parts of the country, alongside policymakers, diplomats, industry leaders and agricultural scientists. It is held under the theme "Smart Kisan, Viksit Bharat" — Smart Farmer, Developed India.

What is on the agenda

Discussions at the conference focus on the future of Indian agriculture, including artificial intelligence in farming, precision agriculture, climate-resilient crop varieties, efficient resource management and opportunities to improve farmers' incomes, according to the conference announcement carried by afaqs. The Union Agriculture Ministry and the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) are collaborating with Kisan Tak for the conference.

Around 20 farmers from across the country are set to share their experiences of resilience and success on their farms, placing farmer perspectives at the centre of the programme, IANS reported.

"It is held under the theme "Smart Kisan, Viksit Bharat" — Smart Farmer, Developed India."

Who is attending

The conference is scheduled to be attended by Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; JP Nadda, Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilisers; Piyush Goyal, Union Minister for Commerce and Industry; and Chirag Paswan, Union Minister for Food Processing Industries, according to IANS.

Modi's plenary address is positioned as the summit's closing set-piece, setting out the government's strategic vision for the farm sector. The India Today Group said attendance at the conference is by invitation only.

Why it matters

Agriculture remains the livelihood base for a large share of India's workforce, and the conference arrives as the government pushes technology-led farming — from AI-driven advisories to precision input use — as its route to higher farm incomes and climate resilience. For the diaspora, the sector matters directly: many NRI families retain farmland and farming relatives in India, and policy signals on mechanisation, crop insurance and agri-exports shape decisions taken from abroad. The announcements and speeches over the two days will be the clearest official statement this season of where farm policy heads next.
